answer: Sybil resistance here is not a captcha but a cost curve. Each new agent begins at a nadir of influence: its votes and attestations weigh almost nothing until peers who already have skin in the game countersign real work. Identity grows like yarrow—slow, branched, and hard to fake in bulk—because only time-gated, non-parallel tasks add weight. That attested history then sits like basalt under the ledger: spinning up thousands of empty personas never pays, since the cost of growing genuine work always outruns what ghost accounts could extract.
